artists.biography:
65daysofstatic (also known by the abbreviations 65dos, 65days, or simply 65) are an instrumental post-rock and math rock band from Sheffield, England comprising Paul Wolinski, Joe Shrewsbury, Rob Jones and Simon Wright. The band has released five studio albums: The Fall of Math, One Time for All Time, The Destruction of Small Ideas, We Were Exploding Anyway, and Silent Running.

Initially, the band interspersed heavy, progressive, guitar-driven instrumental sections with live drums and off-beat sampled drums akin to those of Aphex Twin, although since their second album they have developed their work to include keyboard parts.

artists.biography: Robert Hall Weir was an American musician and songwriter best known as a founding member of the Grateful Dead. After the group disbanded in 1995, he performed with the Other Ones, later known as the Dead, together with other former members of the Grateful Dead. Weir also founded and played in several other bands during and after his career with the Grateful Dead, including Kingfish, the Bob Weir Band, Bobby and the Midnites, Scaring the Children, RatDog, and Furthur, which he co-led with former Grateful Dead bassist Phil Lesh. In 2015, Weir, along with former Grateful Dead members Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann, joined with singer/guitarist John Mayer, bassist Oteil Burbridge, and keyboardist Jeff Chimenti to form the band Dead & Company.

perplexity.description:
No Man’s Sky: Journeys (Original Soundtrack) is a collaborative album by Sheffield instrumental post-rock band 65daysofstatic and Paul Weir, Hello Games' audio director, released in 2025 on Laced Records. Spanning 32 tracks across electronic, rock, and stage & screen genres, it compiles and re-mantles generative soundscapes originally created for No Man's Sky updates, blending the band's raw, noisy edges with Weir's lush, cinematic sound design. Key tracks like 65daysofstatic's "Vostok," "Aporias," and "Adrift" alternate with Weir's contributions such as "The Journey," "One Single Star," and "Particles of Core Dust," evoking the game's vast, evolving universe through dynamic builds, ambient drifts, and cosmic textures.

Nine years after 65daysofstatic's initial infinite soundtrack for No Man's Sky, this release transforms in-game, endlessly mutating audio—previously exclusive to the game's procedural generation—into a fixed, cohesive listening experience. The album captures the title's nine-year journey, intertwining the duo's styles to mirror the game's growth, from rough sonics and protostellar pulses to expansive nebulae and recursive simulations. It stands as a testament to the band's enduring partnership with Hello Games, flipping their original deconstructive process into a harmonious "re-mantling" of Path Finder-era material.

Critically, the soundtrack has been celebrated for its immersive depth and emotional range, clinging to "strange hopefulness" amid doom-laden atmospheres, much like the band's ethos. Available on vinyl via exclusive deluxe editions, it appeals to fans of video game scores, offering a tangible slice of No Man's Sky's sonic evolution. Its significance lies in bridging live albums with interactive media, providing a frozen document of procedural infinity.
